tasks.short: Count ward supplies, check expiry, requisition from the central store, send instruments for sterilisation and report delivery errors.

steps.what: Nurse counts supplies in the ward storeroom against the stock list
Nurse checks expiry dates of sterile supplies and removes expired items
Nurse writes the requisition: on a paper form for all items today, in the order form for non-standard items only after the change
Nurse checks the final requisition: items, quantities, the reason for non-standard items and the central store it goes to
Nurse submits the checked requisition; it routes to the charge nurse and, once signed, to the central store
Charge nurse signs requisitions for items outside the standard list
Logistics assistant scans the cards of empty bins on the ward round
Logistics assistant checks the round's refill list: items, quantities and the ward it is for
Logistics assistant releases the checked refill list as a replenishment order in the warehouse system
Logistics assistant delivers the order and fills the shelves
Nurse sends used instruments to sterilisation and tracks their return: by phone today, by reading the set status on the ward screen after the change
Sterilisation assistant scans each instrument set's code as it moves through cleaning and packing
Nurse reports missing or wrong items in the delivery: by phone today, by marking the order lines in the order screen after the change
Nurse checks the error report: the items marked missing or wrong, quantities and the delivery it belongs to
Nurse submits the checked error report to the central store

tasks.design: Standard ward supplies move to two-bin shelves: the logistics assistant scans empty bins on the round, checks the refill list and releases it as a replenishment order in the hospital warehouse system ({OPS_SYSTEM}). The nurse only requisitions non-standard items through a form, checks it and submits it once; it routes to the charge nurse and then to the store. Instrument sets are scanned by the sterilisation department in its tracking system ({OTHER}) with status visible on the ward. Delivery errors are marked on the order lines in the same order screen, checked and submitted once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ward stock was counted by nurses and ordered on paper because no one else owned the storeroom.
tasks.enabler_now: Hospital warehouse systems support two-bin scanning and par levels, and sterilisation departments track instrument sets by scan.
tasks.still_hard: Par levels must fit real use, rarely used items still need checking, and expiry checks stay manual.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which items the ward cannot run out of tonight and spotting damaged sterile packs.
tasks.altitude: The nurse handles exceptions instead of counting shelves; non-standard approvals stay with the charge nurse.

reach.task: Replenish ward stock on a fixed round
reach.learn: Whether scanning bins fits into their rounds without extra time.

evidence.claim: Integrations and a records app can replace paper logs, spreadsheets and phone in data entry and logging tasks.
Hospital warehouse systems support two-bin scanning with par levels, and sterilisation departments track instrument sets by scan.
Medical devices fall under the EU medical device regulation, which also covers traceability duties for some devices.

assumptions: Boundary: from checking ward stock to deliveries and instruments back; purchasing from suppliers is outside.

Input contract: par levels per item set by logistics with the ward's charge nurse; bins scanned by the logistics assistant; instrument set codes scanned by the sterilisation department; fallback is the paper form and phone.
Charge nurse, logistics and sterilisation time is outside the nurse's savings.

Expiry checks, the requisition check and submit, and the error report check and submit keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for non-standard items still counted; s3 keeps 30 because only non-standard items are written; s6 keeps 50 because sending instruments stays and phoning to track them goes; s7 keeps 60 because marking order lines replaces a phone call and the nurse still describes what is wrong. The bin scans, refill check and set scans are other-role time.
unknowns: Whether the ward has a logistics round today.
Share of supplies on the standard list.
research_questions: Do stock-outs on the ward fall after two-bin replenishment?

already_counted.description: Nurse checks the non-standard requisition before it routes.

incremental.description: Nurse reports items whose par level does not fit use.
Logistics keeps par levels and the standard list current.

approvals.approved_version: The requisition with items, quantities and reasons exactly as checked by the nurse in s3b, submitted once to the charge nurse for signature and, signed unchanged, to the central store; any change needs a new check.

The refill list with items and quantities for this ward exactly as checked by the logistics assistant in l2, released once as a replenishment order to the central store in the warehouse system; any change needs a new check.

The error report with the items marked missing or wrong and their quantities exactly as checked by the nurse in s7b, submitted once to the central store for that delivery; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the ward's items fit the bins, so the nurse still counts and writes much of the stock and s1 keeps 70, s3 keeps 65 (27.9); high: standard supplies run on bins as designed (43.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The licensed practical nurse keeps checking what matters on the shelves; counting and paper orders move to logistics and the system.
skills_to_grow: Spotting par levels that do not fit use
role.ambitious_version: A nurse who never counts a storeroom again and still never runs out of what patients need.

job.title: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
